Hand-authored single-cut stereo fixture: 42 small drug-like structures covering a cut-invalidated pseudo stereocentre, surviving tetrahedral centres, retained and re-expressed E/Z geometry, an isotope-labelled centre, created stereocentres, dependent ring stereo in a 1,4-disubstituted cyclohexane pair and a 1,3-disubstituted cyclobutane together with the lone ring tags that must be cleared, a parent stereo tag that describes nothing, an invalid geminal E/Z marker, the three-coordinate nitrogen motifs upstream does not enumerate, three acyclic stereogenic alkenes whose flanking single bonds are both cuttable so that mmpdb reference defect 5 is reached, and the nine structures added for the RDKit tag-retention rules: a ring sulfoxide, a cis-fused decalin, a bicyclo[2.2.2] bridgehead pair, the acyclic pseudo-asymmetric centre of ribitol and the ring one of tropine, a bridgehead nitrogen, an aziridine nitrogen, an indolizidine whose nitrogen tag is cleared, and a three-coordinate phosphine. Two of those nine -- the decalin and the indolizidine -- have no bond outside a ring, so mmpdb's default cut SMARTS matches nothing in them and the oracle is silent about them by construction; they are here for the cleanup rule and are asserted in tests/cpp/test_fragment_smiles.cpp, and test_oracle_covers_every_fixture_structure ties the exemption to that SMARTS rather than to a title list. On created-centre placement: isobutanol_created_frag1 (OCC(C)C) puts the new centre in RDKit fragment 1 for both of its desymmetrising cuts, while ethylbutanol_created_frag2 (CCC(CC)CO) puts it in fragment 2 for cut (1,2) and in fragment 1 for cut (3,2). A fragment-2-only structure cannot exist at one cut: every desymmetrising cut has an automorphic partner cut yielding the same fragment pair with the centre in fragment 1, and mmpdb dedupes on attachment_order.variable_smiles.constant_smiles without the enumeration label, so the partner always restores the row. That is why the accompanying allowlist carries no up-enumeration rows.

mmpdb 3.1.4 single-cut oracle, regenerated 2026-09-10 when the fixture grew from 33 to 42 structures with the ring sulfoxide, ring-fusion, bridgehead, heteroatom and pseudo-asymmetric structures; the 33 earlier titles' rows came back byte-identical to the previous generation, as the 30 titles before them had at the regeneration that added the acyclic stereogenic alkenes and the 21 original titles had at the 2026-09-09 one before that. Generated with `mmpdb fragment tests/data/mmpdb/stereo_cases.smi --num-cuts 1 -o stereo.fragdb` then `sqlite3 -header -tabs stereo.fragdb "SELECT record.title AS molecule_id, fragmentation.num_cuts, fragmentation.enumeration_label, fragmentation.variable_num_heavies, fragmentation.variable_smiles, fragmentation.attachment_order, fragmentation.constant_num_heavies, fragmentation.constant_smiles, coalesce(fragmentation.constant_with_H_smiles, '') as constant_with_h_smiles FROM fragmentation JOIN record ON record.id = fragmentation.record_id ORDER BY record.title, fragmentation.enumeration_label, fragmentation.variable_smiles, fragmentation.constant_smiles;"`. Complete as generated: no rows were filtered. Two of the 42 titles -- decalin_cis_fusion_pair and indolizidine_nitrogen_cleared -- contribute no rows because every bond in each is a ring bond, which mmpdb's default cut SMARTS never matches. It contains no `[*][H]` hydrogen fragmentations (mmpdb fragment_algorithm._hydrogen_cut_smiles) because `mmpdb fragment` drives fragment_mol, which never calls get_hydrogen_fragmentations; that absence is pinned structurally by test_oracle_contains_no_hydrogen_cut_rows rather than worked around.

It holds exactly the twelve reference-defect-5 rows for the three acyclic stereogenic alkenes, four per structure because the one cut mmpdb inverts appears in both orientations and in both directions; OEMMPA reproduces every other mmpdb record for this fixture.
